chunks.text: Maize is the primary staple crop in Korogwe District, Tanga Region. Two main planting seasons exist: long rains (Masika) from March to May and short rains (Vuli) from October to December. The long rains season produces higher yields due to more consistent rainfall. Optimal planting should begin when cumulative rainfall reaches 100mm over 10 days, typically mid-March for long rains. Late planting after mid-April reduces yield potential by 20-40%.

Recommended maize varieties for Korogwe include SEEDCO SC403 (120 days to maturity, high yield potential 4-6 tons/acre), DK8031 (110 days, drought tolerant), and Pioneer P3812W (115 days, good disease resistance). Local open-pollinated varieties mature in 140-160 days but yield only 1-2 tons/acre under low input management. Hybrid varieties require 20-25 kg seed per acre planted at 75cm x 25cm spacing (approximately 21,000 plants per acre).

Fertilizer schedule for maize in Korogwe: At planting (basal), apply 50 kg DAP (18:46:0) per acre or 50 kg NPK 20:10:10 per acre. Place fertilizer 5cm below and 5cm beside the seed. At 4-6 weeks after planting (V6 stage), top dress with 50 kg CAN (26% N) per acre applied in a band 10cm from the plant row. Second top dressing at tasseling if soil is fertile: 25 kg CAN per acre.

Common maize pests in Korogwe: Fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) — larvae feed on leaves and whorl, economic threshold is 20% plant damage. African stem borer (Busseola fusca) — larvae tunnel into stems causing deadheart. Maize weevil (Sitophilus zeamais) — post-harvest storage pest. African armyworm (Spodoptera exempta) — seasonal outbreaks during short rains. Scout fields weekly from 2 weeks after emergence.

Common maize diseases in Korogwe: Grey leaf spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis) — favored by warm humid conditions, 26-30°C with >85% humidity. Maize streak virus — transmitted by leafhoppers, causes streaking. Downy mildew (Sclerophthora macrospora) — waterlogged fields. Northern corn leaf blight (Exserohilum turcicum) — cool wet conditions. Stalk rot — late season, lodging risk. Maize lethal necrosis — notifiable, contact TVLA.

IPM options for maize: Cultural controls include crop rotation with legumes (beans, cowpeas), early planting to avoid peak pest pressure, destroying crop residues after harvest, and intercropping with beans or cowpeas. Biological controls: Trichogramma wasps for stem borer egg parasitism, Beauveria bassiana for fall armyworm. Chemical controls: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5EC at 20ml per 20L knapsack for armyworm, Deltamethrin 2.5EC at 15ml per 20L for stem borer. Always follow PHI (pre-harvest interval).

Maize growth stages and day counts from planting: Germination (5-10 days), Emergence (7-14 days), Vegetative V1-V12 (14-60 days), Tasseling VT (60-70 days), Silking R1 (65-75 days), Grain fill R2-R3 (75-100 days), Dent R4 (100-110 days), Maturity R5 (110-130 days). Harvest when grain moisture is 20-25% or when husks are dry and brown. Dry to 13% moisture for safe storage.

Yield benchmarks for maize in Korogwe: Low input (no fertilizer, local variety, rainfed only): 0.8-1.5 tons per acre. Medium input (hybrid variety, DAP + one CAN top dress, 25kg seed): 2.5-3.5 tons per acre. High input (improved hybrid, full fertilizer schedule, irrigation supplement, pest control): 4-6 tons per acre. Average smallholder yield in Tanga is 1.2 tons per acre — significant room for improvement with proper inputs.

Silage maize production: Plant denser at 30,000 plants per acre (75cm x 20cm). Harvest at 50% grain moisture or when kernel milk line is 50% (approximately 90-100 days). Chop to 2-3cm pieces. Add molasses at 2% of fresh weight to improve fermentation. Pack tightly in pit silo, cover with plastic sheet, seal with soil. Fermentation takes 21-28 days. Quality indicators: pleasant vinegar smell, olive-green colour, temperature <35°C, pH 3.8-4.2. Safe to feed after 28 days.
